questions.title: Build a Binary Tree and Print Preorder
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Build linked tree nodes from level-order input and visit them in preorder.
questions.problem_statement:
Build a binary tree from its level-order representation. Print its preorder traversal: visit the root, then the left subtree, then the right subtree. Create your own linked tree nodes.

Tree input rule: N counts every entry, including -1 markers. The first entry is the root and is not -1 when N > 0. Process the present nodes in level order; for each one, read the next two entries as its left and right children. An entry of -1 means that child is missing, and missing nodes have no child entries. If the entries run out, the remaining children are missing. No entries are left over, and N = 0 means the tree is empty.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, such as a Node class, without the public keyword.

![M18-01 — Build a Binary Tree and Print Preorder](/diagrams/m18/m18_01.png)

Explanation: Visit 1 first, then its left subtree (2, 4, 5), and then its right subtree (3, 6).
questions.input_format: N, followed by N level-order entries.
questions.output_format: Print the preorder values separated by single spaces. If the tree is empty, print an empty line.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 100,000
Actual values fit in int and cannot be -1.
Tree height ≤ 1,000.
hints: Build the tree with a queue: each node taken from the queue receives the next two entries as its children.
Only add a child to the queue when its entry is not -1.
Preorder is recursive: print the node, then recurse left, then recurse right.

Tree input rule: N counts every entry, including -1 markers. The first entry is the root and is not -1 when N > 0. Process the present nodes in level order; for each one, read the next two entries as its left and right children. An entry of -1 means that child is missing, and missing nodes have no child entries. questions.title: Validate a Binary Search Tree
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Check the BST property using value bounds inherited from all ancestors.
questions.problem_statement:
Determine whether a binary tree satisfies the strict BST property: every value in a node's left subtree must be smaller than the node's value, and every value in its right subtree must be larger. Duplicate values make the tree invalid. An empty tree is valid.

Check all ancestor bounds, not just immediate parent-child relationships. Use bounds that work correctly for values near the int limits.

Tree input rule: N counts every entry, including -1 markers. The first entry is the root and is not -1 when N > 0. Process the present nodes in level order; for each one, read the next two entries as its left and right children. An entry of -1 means that child is missing, and missing nodes have no child entries. If the entries run out, the remaining children are missing. No entries are left over, and N = 0 means the tree is empty.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, such as a Node class, without the public keyword.

![M18-10 — Validate a Binary Search Tree](/diagrams/m18/m18_10.png)

Explanation: Node 10 is in the left subtree of 8 but is greater than 8, which violates the BST property even though 10 is a valid right child of 4.
questions.input_format: N, followed by N level-order entries.
questions.output_format: Print VALID if the tree is a strict BST; otherwise, print INVALID.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 100,000
Actual values fit in int and cannot be -1.
Tree height ≤ 1,000.
hints: Comparing each node only with its parent is not enough.
Pass down an allowed open range (low, high); going left sets high to the node's value, and going right sets low.
Use long bounds starting at Long.MIN_VALUE and Long.MAX_VALUE so nodes holding Integer.MIN_VALUE or Integer.MAX_VALUE are handled correctly.

Insert N distinct integers into a BST in the given order, then delete X. If X has zero or one child, remove it and connect its child, if any, to its parent. If X is absent, leave the tree unchanged.

questions.title: Build a Max Heap
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Build a heap in O(N) time with bottom-up sift-down instead of repeated insertion.
questions.problem_statement:
Build a max heap from the given array using bottom-up heap construction, not sequential insertion. Every parent must be greater than or equal to its children. For index i, the children are at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2.

Process parent indices from N / 2 − 1 down to 0, applying sift-down to each. During sift-down, swap only when a child is strictly greater than the parent. If both children are equal and greater than the parent, choose the left child.

Input hint: When N = 0, the values line may be empty or omitted, so read the input token by token.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, such as a Node class, without the public keyword.

![M18-13 — Build a Max Heap](/diagrams/m18/m18_13.png)

Explanation: Index 1 holds 2, and its larger child is 5, so they swap. Index 0 holds 1; it swaps with 5 and then with 4, giving 5 4 3 1 2. Inserting the values one at a time would produce 5 4 2 1 3 instead.
questions.input_format: N, followed by N integers.
questions.output_format: Print the heap's internal array representation, separated by single spaces. Print an empty line when N = 0.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 200,000
Values fit in int.
hints: Leaves are already valid heaps, so start from the last parent at index N / 2 − 1.
Sift-down: compare the node with its children, swap with the larger child if that child is strictly greater, and continue from the child's index.
Check the left child first and replace it only when the right child is strictly greater; this applies the tie rule automatically.

questions.title: Find the Running Median of a Data Stream
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Maintain the lower and upper halves of a stream with two balanced heaps.
questions.problem_statement:
Integers arrive one at a time. After each insertion, report the median of all values received so far.

Use a max heap for the lower half and a min heap for the upper half. Keep the lower heap the same size as the upper heap or one element larger. For an odd number of values, the median is the lower heap's root. For an even number, it is the average of both heap roots.

Output hint: Convert the roots to long before adding them so the sum cannot overflow. If you use String.format, pass Locale.US so the decimal separator is a dot; for 200,000 lines, a StringBuilder is much faster than printing each line separately.

![M18-14 — Find the Running Median of a Data Stream](/diagrams/m18/m18_14.png)

Explanation: After 5 and 2 arrive, the sorted values are 2 and 5, so the median is 3.5. After all five values arrive, the sorted values are 2 4 5 8 10, so the median is 5.0.
questions.input_format: N, followed by N integers in arrival order.
questions.output_format: Print N medians, one per line, with exactly one digit after the decimal point and a dot as the decimal separator.

1 ≤ N ≤ 200,000
Values fit in int.
hints: Insert into the lower (max) heap if the value is at most its root; otherwise, insert into the upper (min) heap.
After each insertion, move one root across if the size rule is broken.
Adding two int roots can overflow; compute ((long) a + b) / 2.0.

questions.title: Serialize and Deserialize a Binary Tree
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Encode a tree's full structure with null markers and rebuild it from the encoding.
questions.problem_statement:
Serialize the input tree in preorder: root, left subtree, right subtree. Output # for each missing child. Then reconstruct a new tree from that serialization and print the reconstructed tree's inorder traversal.

A tree with T actual nodes produces exactly 2T + 1 serialization tokens.

Tree input rule: N counts every entry, including -1 markers. The first entry is the root and is not -1 when N > 0. Process the present nodes in level order; for each one, read the next two entries as its left and right children. An entry of -1 means that child is missing, and missing nodes have no child entries. If the entries run out, the remaining children are missing. No entries are left over, and N = 0 means the tree is empty.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, such as a Node class, without the public keyword.

![M18-16 — Serialize and Deserialize a Binary Tree](/diagrams/m18/m18_16.png)

Explanation: Node 2 has two missing children, written as # #, and so does node 3. Reconstructing the serialization gives the original tree, whose inorder traversal is 2 1 3.
questions.input_format: N, followed by N level-order entries.
questions.output_format: Print the preorder serialization on the first line and the reconstructed tree's inorder traversal on the second line. For an empty tree, print # on the first line and an empty second line.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 100,000
Actual values fit in int and cannot be -1.
Tree height ≤ 1,000.
hints: Serialization is a preorder traversal that writes # instead of returning silently at null.
To deserialize, read tokens with a shared index: # returns null; otherwise, create a node and build its left and then its right subtree.
Print the inorder traversal of the rebuilt tree, not the original one, so the reconstruction is actually tested.

questions.title: Find the Diameter of a Binary Tree
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Compute the longest path in O(N) by combining subtree heights in one postorder pass.
questions.problem_statement:
Find the diameter of a binary tree, defined as the maximum number of edges on any path between two nodes. The path does not have to pass through the root.

Compute the result in O(T) time, where T is the number of actual nodes, by combining subtree heights during a postorder traversal. An empty tree or a single-node tree has diameter 0.

Tree input rule: N counts every entry, including -1 markers. The first entry is the root and is not -1 when N > 0. Process the present nodes in level order; for each one, read the next two entries as its left and right children. An entry of -1 means that child is missing, and missing nodes have no child entries. If the entries run out, the remaining children are missing. No entries are left over, and N = 0 means the tree is empty.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, such as a Node class, without the public keyword.

![M18-17 — Find the Diameter of a Binary Tree](/diagrams/m18/m18_17.png)

Explanation: The path 4 → 2 → 1 → 3 → 6 contains five nodes and therefore four edges.
questions.input_format: N, followed by N level-order entries.
questions.output_format: Print the diameter in edges.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 100,000
Actual values fit in int and cannot be -1.
Tree height ≤ 1,000.
hints: The longest path through a given node uses left height + right height edges, where height counts nodes.
Return the height from each recursive call and update a global best diameter along the way.
Do not call a separate height function for every node; that makes the solution O(N²).

questions.title: Recover a BST with Two Swapped Values
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Find the two out-of-order values in an inorder traversal and swap them back.
questions.problem_statement:
A BST originally contained distinct values, but exactly two node values were swapped. Restore the BST by swapping those two values back without changing the tree structure. The input is guaranteed to be recoverable by one swap.

The swapped values may be adjacent or far apart in the inorder sequence.

Tree input rule: N counts every entry, including -1 markers. The first entry is the root and is not -1 when N > 0. Process the present nodes in level order; for each one, read the next two entries as its left and right children. An entry of -1 means that child is missing, and missing nodes have no child entries. If the entries run out, the remaining children are missing. No entries are left over, and N = 0 means the tree is empty.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, such as a Node class, without the public keyword.

![M18-18 — Recover a BST with Two Swapped Values](/diagrams/m18/m18_18.png)

Explanation: The inorder sequence is 1 3 2, which is not increasing. Swapping 3 and 2 restores the sorted inorder sequence 1 2 3.
questions.input_format: N, followed by N level-order entries.
questions.output_format: Print the corrected BST's inorder traversal, with values separated by single spaces.
questions.constraints:
N ≤ 100,000
The tree contains at least two actual nodes.
Actual values fit in int and cannot be -1.
Tree height ≤ 1,000.
hints: Track the previously visited node during inorder traversal; a drop occurs when prev.val > cur.val.
At the first drop, the first misplaced node is prev. At every drop, update the second misplaced node to cur.
If the swapped values are adjacent, there is only one drop; your logic must still work.

questions.title: Find the Kth Largest Element in a Data Stream
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Track the K largest values of a stream with a bounded min heap.
questions.problem_statement:
Integers arrive one at a time. After each insertion, report the Kth largest value among all values received so far. If fewer than K values have arrived, report NONE. Duplicate values count as separate occurrences.

A min heap holding at most K values is sufficient. Input values may include -1; it has no special meaning in this problem.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, such as a Node class, without the public keyword.

![M18-19 — Find the Kth Largest Element in a Data Stream](/diagrams/m18/m18_19.png)

Explanation: After the first two insertions, fewer than three values exist. After 8 arrives, the third-largest value is 4. It stays 4 after 2 arrives, becomes 5 after 10 arrives, and becomes 8 after 9 arrives.
questions.input_format: The first line contains N and K. The second line contains N integers in arrival order.
questions.output_format: Print N answers on one line, separated by single spaces. The i-th answer is the Kth largest value after the first i insertions, or NONE if fewer than K values have arrived.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ K ≤ N ≤ 200,000
Values fit in int.
hints: Keep only the K largest values seen so far in a min heap.
After adding a value, remove the heap's root if the heap holds more than K values.
When the heap holds exactly K values, its root is the Kth largest.

questions.title: Find the Maximum Sum of a BST Subtree
questions.module: Module 18: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Heaps
questions.objective: Combine validity, range, and sum information from both subtrees in one postorder pass.
questions.problem_statement:
Find the maximum sum among all valid, non-empty BST subtrees of a binary tree. A subtree consists of a node and all of its descendants. A subtree is a valid BST when its left and right subtrees are both valid BSTs, every value in its left subtree is smaller than its root, and every value in its right subtree is larger.

Use postorder traversal to determine each subtree's validity, minimum, maximum, and sum. The answer is the maximum of 0 and all valid non-empty subtree sums, so an empty tree, or a tree whose valid subtree sums are all negative, produces 0.

Tree input rule: N counts every entry, including -1 markers. The first entry is the root and is not -1 when N > 0. Process the present nodes in level order; for each one, read the next two entries as its left and right children. An entry of -1 means that child is missing, and missing nodes have no child entries. If the entries run out, the remaining children are missing. No entries are left over, and N = 0 means the tree is empty.

Write all classes in Main.java. Only class Main may be declared public; declare any other classes, such as a Node class, without the public keyword.

![M18-20 — Find the Maximum Sum of a BST Subtree](/diagrams/m18/m18_20.png)

Explanation: The entire tree is a valid BST, and its sum is 5 + 2 + 8 + 1 + 3 + 6 + 9 = 34.
questions.input_format: N, followed by N level-order entries.
questions.output_format: Print the maximum sum.
questions.constraints:
0 ≤ N ≤ 100,000
Actual values fit in int and cannot be -1.
Tree height ≤ 1,000.
Use long for subtree sums.
hints: For each node, return four facts about its subtree: whether it is a BST, its minimum, its maximum, and its sum.
A node forms a BST only if both children do, the left maximum is smaller than the node, and the right minimum is larger.
Treat an empty subtree as a BST with minimum +∞ and maximum −∞ so leaves need no special case.

extra_fields.output_format: Print the maximum sum.
